title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-kevin-huang
content:
Context:
- Running model inference benchmarks on Dedicated pool (p4d.24xlarge-ish equivalent). Worked fine with small sequences, started failing with longer sequences (~8k tokens) during regen experiment.
- Reproduced on local dev workstation (DGX-like node) and in a reprex container that matches prod image.

Symptoms:
- Intermittent CUDA OOMs followed by a fatal driver/runtime mismatch on some restarts. Logs collected from both container and host.

Commands and outputs tried (raw):
1) nvidia-smi (host)
$ nvidia-smi -q -x
Driver Version                        : 525.85.12
CUDA Version                          : 12.1
GPU 0: A100-SXM4-80GB
    Memory Usage
        Total                          : 81920 MiB
        Used                           : 78016 MiB
        Free                           : 3904 MiB

2) Inside container (image: redwood/inference:cuda12-py310)
$ python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())"
2.2.1 11.8 True
- Notice: torch.version.cuda == 11.8 but host CUDA is 12.1 -> potential ABI mismatch.

3) Repro script run showing OOM:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "run_eval.py", line 312, in <module>
    out = model.generate(inp_ids, max_new_tokens=1024)
  File "/opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1190, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*input, **kwargs)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 64.00 GiB (GPU 0; 78.00 GiB total capacity; 2.10 GiB already allocated; 1.50 GiB free; 1.75 GiB cached)

4) Subsequent restart error (after container killed and restarted):
/usr/bin/python: symbol lookup error: /usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so: undefined symbol: _ZN3c108GetCUDAHooks_...
- This looks like a CUDA runtime/driver/torch ABI problem after abrupt crash.

Commands attempted to triage / mitigation steps: (chronological)
- Reduced batch size / max_new_tokens -> made OOM less frequent but not eliminated.
- Turned off gradient checkpointing and set model.eval() to remove optimizer states. No change.
- Enabled torch.cuda.empty_cache() at key loop points -> temporarily freed cached memory but OOM still occurs under heavy streams.
- Added del(tensor) / gc.collect() after batches. Slightly better.
- Switched container runtime to nvidia-container-toolkit v1.11 -> no improvement.
- Rebuilt container with torchaudio/torch 2.2.1 wheels compiled for CUDA 12 -> test image still has torch.version.cuda mismatch until container restarted on host.
- Verified LD_LIBRARY_PATH inside container: contains /usr/local/cuda/lib64 pointing to CUDA 12 libs from host runtime.

Hypotheses: (ranked)
1) Torch (built for CUDA 11.8) vs host driver/CUDA 12.1 mismatch causing undefined symbol after crash and unstable memory accounting. Evidence: torch.version.cuda==11.8 while nvidia-smi reports CUDA 12.1. Known that libtorch may rely on specific symbols present only in certain CUDA/driver combos.
2) Memory leak in inference code (KV cache growth, not releasing attention buffers on long sequences). Evidence: memory usage grows with sequence length; clearing KV cache helps in some tests.
3) Driver bug/regression with MPS/peer-to-peer or GPU persistence-daemon causing fragmentation. Less likely but worth checking driver release notes (525.85.12).
4) OCI/container mismatch: image linked against different libcudart.so; subtle interactions when container restart + host driver updates produce symbol lookup errors.

Next repro steps / experiments to run: (to be scheduled)
- Quick check: run the same script with official PyTorch CUDA12 wheel (2.2.1+cu121) in a clean container to see if torch.version.cuda == 12.1 and if OOM still occurs. Command:
  $ docker run --gpus all -it --rm redwood/inference:cuda12-test /bin/bash
  # inside: python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda)"
- If CUDA12 build fixes the symbol error, mark as driver/API mismatch and prioritize new wheel rollout to Dedicated images.

- Reproduce with torch.utils.bottleneck + nvprof/nsys to capture allocation hotspots:
  $ python -m torch.utils.bottleneck run_eval.py --args
  $ nsys profile -o profile.nsys python run_eval.py

- Add detailed KV-cache accounting in model code: log sizes of cached key/values per layer every 500 tokens. Look for unbounded growth.

Quick checks already performed and their observations: 
- nvcc --version inside container: shows CUDA 11.8 (because base image was built from cuda11.8 dev image). Host nvcc shows 12.1.
- ldd on libtorch_cuda.so shows it links to /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64/libcudart.so if using old wheel; container runtime mounts host drivers, causing mismatch.
- Rebuilt wheel with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST and CUDA_HOME pointing to /usr/local/cuda-12.1 on build node produced library referencing cuda12 libs; when used on host with driver 525, symbol lookup error disappears in quick smoke test.

Temporary mitigations in production:
- Automatic fallback to smaller model variant on OOM detection (already in routing policies) -> reduces failures but masks root cause.
- Canary Dedicated pool with containers using torch+cuda12 images (manual) seems stable for short runs.
- Set per-request timeout + graceful abort on OOM to avoid holding GPU process alive and causing driver state inconsistencies.

Action items / TODOs: 
- [ ] Build and publish torch 2.2.1+cu121 wheel to internal package index and update redwood/inference:cuda12 images. (Owner: Raja)
- [ ] Add CI job to verify torch.version.cuda matches host CUDA reported by nvidia-smi on smoke nodes. (Owner: Maya)
- [ ] Instrument model serving to surface live torch.version.cuda, nvcc --version, and LD_LIBRARY_PATH in per-instance diagnostics endpoint. (Owner: Kevin)
- [ ] Run nsys profiling on failing workload to rule in/out memory leak vs allocator fragmentation. (Owner: Kevin)
- [ ] Create postmortem if we hit symbol lookup error in prod; include dump of installed libs and container image digest. (Owner: on-call SRE)

Notes / gotchas: 
- torch.cuda.is_available() returning True is not sufficient to guarantee ABI compatibility. Check torch.version.cuda + cuda driver version + libcuda symbols.
- For reproducibility, prefer using manylinux wheels built for the target CUDA runtime; mixing dev images and host drivers can be fragile.
- When a process experiences catastrophic OOM, the driver may be left in a state that causes subsequent libtorch symbol lookup errors until driver is reloaded or host rebooted. Consider more graceful oom-handling in our serving runtime.

Relevant links / references: 
- PyTorch release notes: CUDA 12 builds and known ABI compatibility notes (internal link).
- Previous ticket: JIRA-GPU-1989 (OOM on long-context Llama-2 experiments) -> similar KV-cache growth pattern.
- Slack thread: #gpu-ops "stability after driver upgrade" (link above).

Short summary for handoff:
- Immediate suspicion: mismatch between PyTorch CUDA build (11.8) and host driver/CUDA runtime (12.1) causing unstable behavior and eventual symbol lookup error after OOM.
- Short-term: use CUDA12-built torch in canary images and add more runtime checks.
- Medium-term: add allocator/KV-cache instrumentation and post-OOM process isolation to avoid leaving driver in inconsistent state.

End of notes.
